question: Which firms have co-developed several robotic construction processes with partners?

answer.answer:
One firm, Firm_060, stands out: it appears as a manufacturer on three separate co-developed robot records in the retrieved material, twice alongside Firm_061 and once in a five-firm grouping. Firm_061 and Firm_082 each appear on two, Firm_082 pairing with a different partner each time, and every other firm in view appears once only. Partnership size varies sharply, from two firms to seven on a single robot, and roles differ: some records name manufacturers and distributors separately, one names developers. These are the eight retrieved records only, so the counts are lower bounds rather than totals, and the record labels these as census robot entries rather than as firms co-developing processes in the questioner's terms.

**Repeat partners in the retrieved records**

Firm_060 is the clearest repeat participant. It is a manufacturer on census_RXM6-4, jointly developed by Firm_168, Firm_060, Firm_008, Firm_009 and Firm_064 [1], on census_RXM6-7 with Firm_061 and Firm_079 [2], and on census_RXM6-6 with Firm_061 [3]. Firm_061 therefore appears twice, both times with Firm_060, which reads as a standing pairing rather than two independent collaborations. Firm_082 also appears twice, but with a different partner each time: with Firm_072 on census_RXM8-3 [4] and with Firm_003 on census_RXM8-1 [5].

All other firms in view appear on a single record each, including the seven-firm grouping on census_RXM23-5 (Firm_177, Firm_002, Firm_018, Firm_068, Firm_094, Firm_134, Firm_209) [6], the pair on census_RXH8-2 (Firm_097, Firm_098) [7], and the three developers on census_RXH5-4 (Firm_027, Firm_028, Firm_033) [8].

**Roles are not uniform across these records**

The graph distinguishes the relations. On census_RXM6-4, Firm_008, Firm_060 and Firm_168 are linked by hasManufacturer while Firm_009 and Firm_064 are linked by hasDistributor [9], so two of the five partners on that record are in a distribution role rather than a making one. By contrast, census_RXH5-4 links Firm_027, Firm_028 and Firm_033 by developedBy [9], and the remaining records use hasManufacturer throughout. Anyone counting partnerships should keep those relations apart rather than treating every named firm as a co-developer.

**The deployed record behind one of them**

Only one of these census entries connects upward to a process record: census_RXM6-4 isCensusRecordOf RP14, and RP14 hasCensusRecord census_RXM6-4 [9]. The firms behind it are Firm_060, Firm_008 and Firm_168 as manufacturers, with Firm_009 and Firm_064 distributing. What the machine actually did is not in the retrieved material: no task, no technology readiness level and no enabler drawn on by this record is given, so I cannot say what RP14 performed on site. Two of the other records carry a material: census_RXM6-7 and census_RXM6-6 both use steel, and census_RXH8-2 uses timber [9], which is the only indication of work domain available here.

**What the cited literature layer says about collaboration, and what it does not**

None of these census records is linked in the retrieved material to any of the 140 enablers, so how many cases draw on an enabler cannot be read off them. The dependency layer does carry the organisational side of the question in its own terms. 14 of the 50 coded cases draw on CO11 "Early contractor involvement" (Condition) [10] and 25 draw on CO10 "Vertical integration" (Condition) [10]; both run upstream into the integrated process, since CO10 enablesCapability AT12 "Integrated design-DFAB process", carried by 14 of the 50 [10] and CO11 enablesCapability AT12, carried by 10 of the 50 [10], with AT12 hasPrecondition CO10 on the mirroring argument that technically interdependent systems require tighter organisational coupling such as a single firm, carried by 14 of the 50 [10]. That is a finding about coupling inside one organisation, which is not the same thing as the multi-firm manufacturing partnerships above, and the retrieved material does not connect the two.

The nearest actor enabler is AC8 "DFAB contractor" (Actor), drawn on by 25 of the 50 coded cases [10], and it carries no dependency edges at all [10], which is consistent with the sparsity noted for that category: 88% of Actors have no cited edge [10]. So the co-development relationships visible in the census records have no counterpart in the cited literature layer; they are evidenced by the records themselves.
